pr_title: Add ability for gameplay leaderboard scroll when too many users are displayed
pr_body:
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/129154878-b1484a70-677a-46df-9bb2-be65af9bda85.mp4

Closes #14206.

Currently set to 8 players at one, which seems to be a reasonable number. In the future, the height of this will likely be adjustable in the skin editor. At that point, the logic will need to change slightly (but shouldn't be a huge deal of work).

issue_context.title: Only show top x users in gameplay leaderboard
issue_context.body:
With the new team versus display, it is more important than before to stop this leaderboard from containing every user in the game (and causing the score display to fall off the bottom of the screen).

The leaderboard should probably only show the top x performers in addition to the local user.

review_comments:
```suggestion
                float scrollTarget = scroll.GetChildPosInContent(trackedScore) + trackedScore.DrawHeight / 2 - scroll.DrawHeight / 2;
                scroll.ScrollTo(Math.Clamp(scrollTarget, 0, scroll.ScrollableExtent), false);
```

Changes the gameplay leaderboard to not scroll beyond the scrollable limits. This allows the effect of the tracked user climbing up to a static top, rather than continuing scrolling the leaderboard beyond 0 making the player at the center even when at number one, and only displaying half of the maximum displayable players.

Also makes the user look more like it's climbing when at the bottom.

before:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/129415990-567f4175-cb43-4102-9557-54fc70eff3c5.mp4


after:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/129415736-8b6043ac-e430-41cb-81b5-c46c592dd129.mp4

Although that makes the scroll to the top not smooth due to being clamped to `0`, I have tried enabling scroll animation but that seems to make the leaderboard a bit too wiggly when scrolling in the middle of the scores.
I think the proposal above is what may eventually be desired but it looks bad as provided. So I'm personally leaning towards getting this pull in as is and working on the above as a follow up.
Fair, doesn't seem to be too annoying currently so can be left for a follow-up.

It's definitely what we want, but let's leave it as a follow up. One would hope it's a bit smoother in transition (some heuristic would need to be added to decide whether to send `animated` or not, based on the target position).
